purpose: Stream processing pipeline that consumes network logs from FortiMail, extracts entities into a property-graph stored in DuckDB, computes analytical signals via tiered derived tables and graph algorithms, and trains ML classifiers to produce a spam entity list.

domain_model.description: A property graph of network entities (domains, hosts, subnets, URIs, email templates, text/image content, clusters) connected by co-occurrence and structural edges, with traffic counters and derived analytical signals per node.

bounded_contexts.name: Ingestion
bounded_contexts.description: Parses raw FortiMail logs, extracts entities and relationships, publishes to Kafka topics.

ubiquitous_language.slot: A time-based partition of rawLog files identified by a numeric slot_id
ubiquitous_language.day_id: Unix day number (epoch_seconds / 86400) used to group rawLog directories
ubiquitous_language.rawLog: Gzipped FortiMail log file on NFS containing email metadata records

bounded_contexts.name: Graph Storage
bounded_contexts.description: Owns per-entity-type DuckDB files with base tables, traffic history, and derived analytical columns.

ubiquitous_language.traffic: Total message count involving this entity
ubiquitous_language.spam_traffic: Subset of traffic classified as spam by FortiMail verdict
ubiquitous_language.derived: Analytically computed columns (tiers A-G) refreshed periodically from base data

bounded_contexts.name: Classification
bounded_contexts.description: Trains and runs ML models to score entities as spam, produces release lists.

ubiquitous_language.signal: A floating-point spam probability score (-1 to +1) for an entity from an ML model
ubiquitous_language.weighted_sum: Rule-based composite score aggregating multiple signal sources
ubiquitous_language.release: The periodic publication of an entity blocklist based on aggregated scores

stack.runtime: 27 Kafka consumers + REST API + Flight SQL server + classifier scheduler, deployed as k8s Deployments on a single node (vandc-61), each consumer in its own pod with cgroup memory isolation, DuckDB files on XFS PVCs.

groups.name: Ingestion
groups.description: NFS log scanning, message parsing, entity extraction, and Kafka topic production.

groups.name: Graph Engine
groups.description: Kafka consumers that persist entities and edges to DuckDB, plus tiered derived-table refresh and graph algorithms.

groups.name: Query Layer
groups.description: REST API with direct DuckDB access, Flight SQL for analytical queries, CLI client, and MCP server for LLM agents.

groups.name: Classification
groups.description: ML spam classifier with scheduled training, inference, and release pipelines, plus score ingestion from Kafka.

actors.description: FortiMail appliances that write gzipped rawLog files to NFS mounts, organized by day_id and slot_id.
Security analyst who queries the graph via the CLI client or MCP server to investigate spam patterns.
LLM agent (Claude Code) that queries the graph database through the MCP server for automated investigation.
Internal scheduler that triggers periodic classifier jobs (every 30 min), daily dataset refresh (03:00-05:00 UTC), and weekly retrain (Sunday 02:00-04:00 UTC).

components.name: Message Producer
components.description: Scans NFS-mounted rawLog directories, parses FortiMail log files, and publishes parsed messages to the Kafka 'message' topic.

components.name: Entity Extraction
components.description: Consumes parsed messages from Kafka, extracts 9 entity types and relationships, routes entities to per-type Kafka topics, and writes message-entity linkage to DuckDB.

components.name: Node Consumers
components.description: Eleven Kafka consumers (domain, host, subnet, uri, email_address, text, image, content_template, cluster, plus enrichment workers for WHOIS/CT/UCLT) that persist entity records to per-type DuckDB files with traffic history.

components.name: Edge Consumers
components.description: Three Kafka consumers (emailed_with, association, cluster_member) that persist co-occurrence and structural edges to DuckDB with traffic counters.

components.name: Derived Refresh Service
components.description: Batch process that periodically recomputes derived analytical columns (tiers A-G) for all entity types by attaching base DuckDB files read-only and running tiered SQL computations.

components.name: Score Consumer
components.description: Kafka consumer that receives external reference scores and ML signal scores, persisting them to separate DuckDB files for query-time join.

components.name: GraphDB API
components.description: FastAPI REST server providing entity lookup, search, graph traversal, and admin endpoints via direct DuckDB snapshot connections through an EdgePool, with Bearer token authentication and Prometheus metrics.

components.name: Flight SQL Server
components.description: Arrow Flight SQL gRPC server providing analytical SQL query access to all DuckDB snapshot files for the classifier and external tools.

components.name: Graph Client CLI
components.description: Python CLI (Click) and SDK for querying the GraphDB API, with disk cache, Loki logging, and multiple output formats.

components.name: MCP Server
components.description: FastMCP server exposing GraphDB as tools for LLM agents, wrapping the HTTP API for entity lookup, search, graph traversal, and subgraph queries.

components.name: Classifier Scheduler
components.description: Scheduler that runs periodic ML inference (every 30 min), daily dataset refresh, and weekly model retraining as subprocesses, publishing spam scores to Kafka.

flows.name: Log Ingestion to Graph Storage
flows.description: A FortiMail rawLog file is parsed into a message, entities are extracted and routed to per-type Kafka topics, then consumed and persisted to DuckDB.
flows.trigger: New rawLog slot appears on NFS

steps.action: Scans NFS rawLog directories for new slots
steps.transform: Parses FortiMail log format into structured message dicts

steps.data: Parsed message with all fields (IPs, URIs, email addresses, CKMs)

steps.action: Extracts 9 entity types and routes to per-type topics
steps.data: Individual entity records (domain, host, subnet, uri, email_address, text, image, content_template, cluster)
steps.transform: Splits one message into multiple entity records with deduplication keys

steps.action: Builds emailed_with associations and cluster records
steps.data: Co-occurrence pairs and MinHash band hashes

steps.action: Buffers entities and flushes to DuckDB
steps.technology: DuckDB (PyArrow bulk insert, ON CONFLICT upsert)
steps.transform: Merges new records with existing via upsert, updates traffic history

steps.action: Persists edges with traffic counters to DuckDB

flows.name: Derived Table Refresh
flows.description: The derived-refresh service periodically recomputes analytical signals for entities by attaching base DuckDB files and running tiered SQL computations (A through G).
flows.trigger: Periodic cycle (Tier A: 5min, B: 10min, C: 1h, D: 6h, E: 24h, F: once, G: separate batch)

steps.action: Identifies new and stale entities needing recomputation
Runs tier functions (A-F) against batch_keys temp table
steps.data: Traffic aggregations, neighbor signals, reputation lookups, multi-hop traversals
steps.transform: Computes 72 analytical signals per entity from raw base data

steps.action: Bulk upserts results into derived tables
steps.technology: DuckDB (PyArrow temp table + INSERT SELECT ON CONFLICT)

flows.name: ML Classification Cycle
flows.description: Every 30 minutes, the classifier queries entity features via Flight SQL, runs LightGBM inference, and publishes spam scores to Kafka for the score consumer.

steps.action: Queries entity features from graph via Flight SQL
steps.data: Entity feature matrix (SELECT * FROM derived views WHERE traffic >= 10)
Feature matrix to spam probability scores (-1 to +1)

steps.action: Publishes scores to Kafka score.signal topic
steps.data: Score records (entity_type, entity_key, score, source, ts)

flows.name: Entity Lookup Request
flows.description: An analyst queries an entity via the CLI or API, which validates the Bearer token, checks the entity cache, and falls back to direct DuckDB snapshot queries via EdgePool.

steps.condition: Token present and valid in TokenStore cache

steps.branch: true: return cached, false: query EdgePool

steps.action: EdgePool opens direct DuckDB snapshot connection
steps.condition: Snapshot file exists and not locked

steps.action: Queries base + derived tables, joins scores

failure_modes.trigger: NFS mount becomes unreachable or stale

cascade.effect: Cannot scan rawLog directories, no new slots ingested
Kafka consumer starves, no new entities produced

failure_modes.impact: New log data stops flowing into the graph; existing data remains queryable but becomes stale.
recovery: Message producer resumes automatically on next scan cycle

cascade.effect: Consumer poll times out, cannot commit offsets

failure_modes.impact: Entire pipeline halts; no ingestion, no extraction, no scoring. Existing data remains queryable.
detection: pipeline_consumed_total counter stalls across all consumers
recovery: Offsets committed before failure allow resumption

failure_modes.trigger: Multiple processes attempt concurrent write access to the same DuckDB file
failure_modes.impact: Temporary stall in one entity type's processing; retries with exponential backoff typically resolve within seconds.
recovery: Automatic retry with exponential backoff (30 retries, base 50ms, max 2s)
If persistent, retention process may be holding lock — check for concurrent retention runs

failure_modes.trigger: Derived refresh cycle fails or falls behind due to batch size limits

cascade.effect: ML features stale, scores less accurate
Queries return entities with missing or stale derived columns

failure_modes.impact: Spam classification accuracy degrades; entity queries return incomplete analytical signals.
detection: pipeline_derived_max_staleness_seconds gauge exceeds tier interval thresholds
recovery: Check derived-refresh pod logs for tier_computation_failed
Increase batch_size if contention is low

evidence.note: All consumers use stoik's consume() loop with Buffer + Store, flushing to DuckDB on interval or batch threshold.
Entity extraction is a fan-out filter that splits one message into multiple typed entity records routed to separate Kafka topics.
FastAPI application with 15 router modules exposing REST endpoints.
Arrow Flight SQL server on port 8815 for analytical queries.
API uses EntityCache with tiered TTLs warmed by EdgePool. Client uses DiskCache with configurable TTL.
EdgePool manages direct DuckDB connections to all snapshot files, refreshing on mtime change.
Bearer token middleware with DuckDB-backed TokenStore, activation on first use, admin flag for privileged endpoints.
structlog with JSON renderer for Loki ingestion, stdlib bridge for consistency.
140+ prometheus_client usages across 13 files with tiered metrics (consumer loop, entity-specific, enrichment, download, producer, derived).
Sentinel exporter with per-process status gauges and composite pipeline health. K8s liveness/readiness probes on /health.
DuckDB lock contention handled via retry with exponential backoff and jitter across all store and refresh paths.
Custom scheduler with 30-min periodic, daily (03:00-05:00 UTC), and weekly (Sunday 02:00-04:00) windows, subprocess isolation.
LightGBM signed-label regression with dataset export/prepare, training, validation gate, and inference cycles.
Batch refresh with configurable batch sizes, per-tier limits, and backfill mode for new entities.
MCP server wraps the HTTP API as LLM-friendly tools without additional business logic.
Click CLI with 10 command groups (node, search, path, bulk, metadata, health, cache, config, stream).
30+ Kafka topics with defined retention policies, fan-out from entity-extraction to per-type consumers.
Tier intervals (300, 600, 3600, 21600, 86400) and batch limits (50000, 25000) are hardcoded without named constants explaining their derivation.

gaps.relevance: Multiple external dependencies (Kafka, NFS, Redis) with no circuit breaker to prevent cascading retries during sustained outages.
gaps.recommendation: Add circuit breakers around NFS and Redis calls to fail fast during outages instead of retrying indefinitely.

gaps.relevance: External HTTP calls (Prometheus queries in sentinel, WHOIS/DNS enrichment) lack explicit timeout configuration.
gaps.recommendation: Set explicit timeouts on all external HTTP and DNS calls.

gaps.relevance: Multi-stage pipeline with no trace propagation across Kafka topics — debugging end-to-end latency requires correlating log timestamps across consumers.
gaps.recommendation: Add correlation IDs (trace_id) to Kafka messages and propagate through the pipeline.

gaps.relevance: API endpoints use Pydantic via FastAPI for request models, but several route handlers accept raw path parameters without schema validation.
gaps.recommendation: Add Pydantic validators for entity_type path parameters to reject unknown types at the API boundary.

gaps: No distributed tracing or correlation IDs across Kafka topics
No trace_id propagation from ingestion to query

recommended.description: No API versioning prefix on any endpoint — all routes are unversioned, making breaking changes risky for external consumers.
No rate limiting on any endpoint — a single client can saturate the API with expensive graph traversal queries.
Flight SQL gRPC endpoint has no authentication — any pod in the cluster can execute arbitrary SQL against all DuckDB snapshots.

minor.description: Inconsistent entity type naming across API paths: some use underscores (uri_template), some use hyphens in deploy (content-template).

gateway.notes: Most handlers delegate to EdgePool for data access, but some (search, subgraph) contain inline DuckDB SQL construction.

hexagonal.notes: Handlers import DuckDB connections directly via EdgePool rather than through a service/repository layer. Business logic (neighbor traversal, path finding) lives in route handlers.

debt.interpretation: Moderate debt driven by missing resilience patterns around external dependencies and unauthenticated Flight SQL access. The pipeline is operationally mature with strong observability but lacks circuit breakers and distributed tracing.

violations.detail: Flight SQL server accepts arbitrary SQL queries from any pod in the cluster with no authentication.

violations.anti_pattern: No circuit breaker on external dependencies
violations.detail: Kafka and NFS calls retry indefinitely without circuit breaker protection — a sustained outage causes all consumers to spin on retries.

violations.anti_pattern: Missing timeout on external health probe queries
violations.detail: Sentinel health checks query Prometheus and per-process metrics endpoints without explicit timeouts.
Several route handlers construct inline DuckDB SQL and execute graph traversal logic directly rather than delegating to a service layer.
Multiple hardcoded file paths (/mnt/nfs/rawLog, /opt/data/graph/...) scattered across modules instead of centralized configuration.
All 16 endpoints are unversioned, making breaking changes risky for consumers.
Tier intervals and batch limits are hardcoded numeric literals without documentation of their derivation.

recommendations.title: Add authentication to Flight SQL
recommendations.description: Flight SQL accepts arbitrary SQL with no auth. Add token-based authentication or limit to specific service accounts via NetworkPolicy.

recommendations.title: Add circuit breakers around NFS and Redis
recommendations.description: Wrap NFS and Redis calls with circuit breakers so sustained outages fail fast instead of spinning all consumers on retries.
fixes: No circuit breaker on external dependencies

recommendations.title: Add distributed tracing with correlation IDs
recommendations.description: Propagate a trace_id through Kafka message headers so end-to-end latency can be tracked from ingestion to query.
fixes: No circuit breaker on external dependencies

recommendations.title: Extract graph logic from route handlers
recommendations.description: Move DuckDB SQL construction and graph traversal logic into a service layer so handlers only translate HTTP to domain calls.

recommendations.title: Centralize file path configuration
recommendations.description: Move hardcoded paths (/mnt/nfs/rawLog, /opt/data/graph/...) to a central config module or environment variables.
